Forgejo and Gitea: a config commit a user signed with a GPG key registered on the server verifies with allowedSigners naming the user (Forgejo signer.name, Gitea signer.username) and fails with another name
Forgejo and Gitea: a commit the server signed with its instance key is a platform signature (forgejo-instance): refused by default, verified when allowedSigners lists forgejo-instance
an attestation (another in-toto predicate) signed with the policy key is not an image signature: the ImageVerification waits, and the cosign signature pushed later verifies it
a key Secret without kardinal.io/referenceable: "true" is not read (reason SecretNotReferenceable, nothing promoted); labelling it lets the verification pass
a policy change while the root step waits gives a new ImageVerification (spec immutable, name hashed) and the step waits for it
an image policy with the compact Graph shape: the Pipeline is Ready=False naming it and the Bundle fails with GraphBuildFailed, nothing promoted
hooks with the compact Graph shape: the Pipeline is Ready=False naming hooks and the Bundle fails with GraphBuildFailed, nothing promoted
a pre-hook HookRun deleted while its Job runs: the result is recorded on the step (status.hookRecords) and the HookRun applied again takes it with no second Job; the step promotes
a Bundle's type, pipeline, images, chart, configRef, provenance and intent cannot be updated (API server refuses); metadata stays editable

with --namespace-shard, shard default reconciles namespaces without kardinal.io/shard and shard b those labelled b; each holds the kardinal-shard token Lease of its namespaces and only it reconciles them
relabelling a namespace hands it over: the old shard gives up the token after its in-flight reconciles, the new shard takes it and adopts in-flight promotions (same PR), and back again

a stopped shard keeps its namespace until its heartbeat Lease has not changed for the Lease duration, measured by the taking shard from when it saw it change; then the namespace's new shard takes it over and promotes there
a namespace labelled for a shard no controller runs gets a ShardNotRunning Warning Event from the default shard
a Bundle promotes through a linear chain of the profile's ChainStages environments (100 in full, the API's cap) and every invariant holds
a 120-environment linear chain is accepted and a Bundle promotes through all of it (a compact Graph, #1516)
a fan-out of canary then waves of regions (wave:) promotes each wave after the whole previous wave, with every region of a wave pushing to one branch at once
a 151-environment fan-out (canary, 10 waves of 15 regions) is accepted and promotes (a compact Graph, #1516)
a diamond lattice (layers each depending on the whole layer before, dependsOn) promotes to its exit environment
an environment depending on every one of many parallel environments starts only after the last of them is Verified
a chain mixing auto and pr-review approval promotes two Bundles in turn, one PR per pr-review environment each
several Pipelines writing one repo and branch under their own paths, with Bundles created at once, each end with the newest Bundle Verified and git holding it
the profile's Pipelines (200 in full), each over its own repo, all promote one Bundle created at once
a burst of the profile's BurstBundles (1,000 in full) over many Pipelines settles with the newest Bundle of each Pipeline Verified and the rest Superseded
Bundles created at a sustained rate for a duration (configurable; soak 5/s for 30 min) all settle with the newest of each Pipeline Verified
many Bundles in a row on one Pipeline: the newest ends Verified everywhere and git holds it

Pipeline edits while Bundles are in flight (an environment added and removed, approval switched, health timeout and history limit changed) leave no Bundle stuck, and a Bundle after the edits promotes through the final Pipeline
a PolicyGate opened and closed every two seconds while Bundles promote settles with git holding the last Bundle verified behind it
a blackout ChangeWindow switched on while a prod step waits for merge: the merge completes, a later Bundle gets no prod step until the window ends, then promotes
Pipelines paused and resumed every one to three seconds while Bundles promote settle once resumed
kardinal rollback of an environment while a newer Bundle is mid-chain settles with every environment at the last Bundle verified there
a promotion PR closed and reopened from outside still merges, and a PR merged by a person as its Bundle is superseded leaves the newest Bundle Verified
the Pipeline's branch force-pushed back to its first commit mid-promotion: a later Bundle promotes everywhere on the rewritten branch
a namespace deleted with Bundles in flight and PRs open is gone within three minutes, leaving no open PR or kardinal branch in its repos
forged, duplicate and out-of-order SCM webhooks (merged for an open PR, ten deliveries of one merge, opened after merged, unknown PRs) change nothing; only the real merge advances the step
the controller leader killed with no grace period every 20 to 60 seconds under load: the other replica takes over and every promotion finishes once
the kro controller killed every 45 to 75 seconds under load: Graphs pick up where they were
1.5 s of latency on every git server response under load slows promotions but fails none
two 60-second git server outages under load: promotions wait and retry, and the newest Bundle of every Pipeline ends Verified (known bug #1476)
the controller throttled by API Priority and Fairness to one seat under load still settles every Bundle
the SCM token Secret rotated to another user's token mid-flight: promotions finish and later PRs are the new user's
one Bundle on each of the profile's SLOPipelines Pipelines at once: automatic steps and Bundles stay under the profile's latency objective (known bug #1509 while reconcilers run one worker)

each controller reconciles several objects at once (--promotionstep-workers 16, --prstatus-workers 8, --policygate-workers 8, --bundle-workers 4, --pipeline-workers 4; chart controller.workers): steps of many Pipelines and many gates run side by side without shared state (-race), and Bundles of one Pipeline with maxConcurrentPromotions take their slots under a per-Pipeline lock, never past the cap
a PromotionStep requeues its Pipeline only when it is created or deleted or its state or outputs.noChanges changes, not on every status write

the Graph identity (ServiceAccount, applier and reader RoleBindings) is bound and pruned under a per-namespace lock, and a translation lists the namespace's Graphs to prune only when a recorded reader namespace is no longer read by its Graph

AuditEvent retention (opt-in, --audit-retention): the leader deletes, every --audit-retention-interval, a Pipeline's records past the --audit-retention-max-per-pipeline newest (by creationTimestamp, within a second by created-at) and records created longer ago than --audit-retention-max-age, paged metadata-only lists, at most 2000 a run oldest first, 410 on continue tolerated; chart audit.retention is off by default (no delete grant) and enabled: true passes the flags (90 days, 1000) and grants delete

AuditEvent retention bounds: lists are metadata-only pages of 500, age is metadata.creationTimestamp (a future time is never old) decided while streaming, the count cap lists only a Pipeline past it, newest by creationTimestamp then created-at, deletion oldest first, at most 2000 a run, an expired continue token (410) ends the run without error, and the off switch lists nothing

ScmProvider: a Pipeline's spec.git.providerRef names a ScmProvider in its namespace (type, apiURL, token Secret, allowedRepositories); the provider turns Ready; the translator writes its kind, name and UID into each PromotionStep and the step copies it into its PRStatus; the PR is opened, polled and merged with the provider's token (PR author is the provider's user), not the controller's --scm-provider

feature: ScmProvider webhooks: /webhook/scm/namespaces/<ns>/<name> checks deliveries with the provider's webhookSecretRef and marks only that provider's PRStatuses; the controller's /webhook/scm marks none of them, and the provider's endpoint refuses the controller's secret
ScmProvider: a Bundle whose Pipeline names a ScmProvider that does not exist stays Available with TranslationError naming it, retried every 15s, and promotes once the provider is created

ClusterScmProvider: a Pipeline in a namespace the provider's allowedNamespaces does not select stays Available with TranslationError naming the provider and namespace; once the namespace has the label, the PR is opened with the provider's token, whose Secret may live in any namespace

ClusterScmProvider deleted and created again under the same name (another UID) while a step waits for its PR: the step fails with 'deleted and created again' instead of polling the PR through the new provider

Provider caches and webhook limits: Evict (provider deleted) drops its client and its cached token and webhook Secrets; a cache write drops expired Secrets and Namespaces; the client cache keeps the most recently used clients past its bound; a provider endpoint takes a rate-limit bucket only after the provider is found (LRU of buckets, unknown names never 429), refuses a flood with 429 before its Secret is read again, and never reads the token before the signature is checked (contract: cache internals and read counts are not observable live)

feature: the Graphs deleted in a namespace share one queued prune of its reader RoleBindings (one work-queue key per namespace), so Graph cleanup keeps up with Graph retirement

kardinal reject sets spec.rejected with the SelfSubjectReview username; the Bundle turns Rejected with Ready reason Rejected and a Rejected condition naming user and reason; its WaitingForMerge step fails as rejected, the PR is closed and a PromotionRejected AuditEvent is written; a delivered environment keeps the change and no new step is created
spec.rejected is one-way: the CRD refuses to remove or change it, and kardinal reject refuses a Bundle already rejected
the chart's bundle-rejection ValidatingAdmissionPolicy denies a spec.rejected.by other than the requesting user on create and update, and admits the requester's own
a Bundle that has not finished and carries an image or config commit of a rejected Bundle turns Rejected with reason RejectedArtifact, promotes nothing and supersedes nothing
a reject that lands after the PR merged does not cancel the step: it is health-checked and Verified, and rollback treats it as what the environment runs
kardinal rollback never targets a rejected Bundle, also one Verified in the environment, and rollback --to a rejected Bundle is refused

a rejected image with a digest matches only that digest, so a fixed image pushed under the same moving tag (r/a:latest@fixed after r/a:latest@bad) is promoted, rolled back to and picked up by a Subscription; a rejected image without a digest matches by tag

a Rejected Bundle whose change is live in an environment (step HealthChecking or Verified) stays current there, marked Rejected with the roll-back hint, in DerivePhase (Degraded), currentBundleByEnv, CurrentBundle, kardinal get pipelines/status/explain/get steps/logs and the UI (rejectedLiveEnvironments, RejectedLiveBanner)

historyLimit never deletes a Bundle with spec.rejected, whatever its phase, nor a carrier whose change is live (RejectedLiveEnvs, retired steps included), and may delete other Bundles Rejected only for carrying a rejected artifact

marking a Bundle Rejected records status.rejectedArtifacts: the artifacts that differ from the Bundle Verified before it in each environment it reached (all of them without a predecessor); rollback, promote and Subscriptions match that set, so an unchanged sidecar does not block a rollback to the predecessor; a carrier is marked only from a recorded set; a retired Bundle is rejected too

kardinal override records createdBy as the SelfSubjectReview username; the controller keeps one status.overrides record per override (firstSeen, verified while the identity policy is bound, audited) and writes one GateOverridden AuditEvent stamped firstSeen, with no second record on later evaluations

the chart's gate-overrides ValidatingAdmissionPolicy refuses an override in someone else's name, editing another user's override, creating a gate instance by hand, and any change to a gate instance's spec or metadata (labels, annotations, finalizers) but its overrides by anyone but kro and the controller, cluster admins included

an override counts from firstSeen for at most --gate-override-max-minutes (the gate reason and AuditEvent name the capped end); a future-dated createdAt or a record past 200 is not counted (OverrideIgnored); a removed and re-added entry keeps its record

an approval gate (spec.approval required 2, allowedGroups, excludeAuthor) holds an auto environment with no step and reason "waiting for approvals: N of 2" until two distinct allowed people approved with kardinal approve; then the environment promotes

an approval from someone outside allowedUsers/allowedGroups is recorded in status.approvals but not counted, a counted reject blocks the gate until the approver changes the decision, someone else cannot revoke an Approval, and every decision writes an ApprovalRecorded or ApprovalRevoked AuditEvent
the chart's approvals ValidatingAdmissionPolicy refuses an Approval whose spec.user is not the requesting user or whose groups the requester does not have

while a pr-review PR waits for its merge, the Graph mirrors the environment's gates onto the step (spec.live.gates) and the step posts kardinal/gates on the commit git-push pushed (persisted output pushedSHA, kept as status.outputs.prHeadSHA): success while the gates pass, failure naming the gate when a ChangeWindow starts, success again when it ends; the step keeps waiting and the PR stays open; a commit someone else pushes to the PR branch gets no kardinal/gates status
a PR merged while a gate blocks is not refused: the step is health-checked and Verified, and status.outputs.mergedWhileBlocked names the gate

GitHub, Forgejo/Gitea, GitLab, Bitbucket Cloud and Azure DevOps set the kardinal/gates status on the commit kardinal pushed, without reading the PR head, in their own API's terms (commit status, GitLab name with an unchanged state counted as set, Bitbucket build status, Azure DevOps PR iteration status on the iteration of that commit, none when no iteration has it); the allowlist guard checks and forwards it

a failed kardinal/gates post never fails the step: it is recorded in status.outputs.gatesStatus with a retry time and one GatesStatusFailed Event; transient errors back off from 30s to an hour and a new gate result or commit is tried at once; a permanent 4xx waits an hour keyed on the SCM token identity (a new gate result does not retry, a rotated token does); an Azure DevOps commit with no PR iteration waits an hour or a new push; a missing pushed commit posts nothing with a GatesStatusNoCommit Event; --gates-commit-status=false posts none and --gates-status-context renames it (Helm scm.gatesCommitStatus); only GitHub's 403 JSON message counts as a rate limit, against the shared quota circuit

the graph-objects ValidatingAdmissionPolicy refuses, for a user with full RBAC and for the cluster admin, creating a PromotionStep, setting a step's state, writing spec.live, and marking a PRStatus merged; the promotion is unaffected

a PolicyGate created ahead of kro under a gate instance's name (with a pre-seeded override) is not adopted: kro's update adding kardinal.io/bundle is refused, prod waits, and after deleting it kro creates the instance without the override

graph-objects policy rules per kind: kro and the controller (exact or admission.controllerUsernames, prefix *) may create and update PromotionSteps, PRStatuses, HookRuns, RenderRuns, ImageVerifications, per-promotion MetricCheck instances and their status (no one may turn an existing MetricCheck into an instance); the garbage collector and namespace controller may update; users, cluster admins, other namespaces' Graph ServiceAccounts and other release-namespace ServiceAccounts may not; only labelled AnalysisRuns are protected, on create
